missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C001 (partial): Hypotheses and source variant are not supplied (failure condition: unstated assumption). def:p15-filtration-martingale (body 18-26) defines adaptedness but never requires it. A martingale is therefore any real process with integrable terms and E(X_{n+1}|F_n)=X_n, and sub/supermartingales swap the identity for an inequality. The held source's definition (Durrett PTE5 p. 217) has three conditions, and condition (ii), 'X_n adapted to F_n', is dropped. For sub- and supermartingales the inequality does not imply adaptedness. The handbook's own proofs still rely on it: annex 77 says 'The case n=m follows from adaptedness', annex 91 says 'adaptedness was explicitly assumed', and annex 35/104/124/150/412/559/586/734 check adaptedness. The optional-stopping chapter on the same route states the convention outright (optional-stopping-and-random-walks.tex 12-13). Concrete case: take F_n trivial, X_0=-2-U and X_n=-1 for n>=1. This meets the definition as written, but the n=m case of thm:p15-martingale-conditioning fails.

ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C003 (partial): Promised cases are not written. Body 72-74 promises the reduced-filtration property for all three classes. The annex writes only the supermartingale chain (annex 84-89). The submartingale and martingale cases are dispatched with 'The sign-reversed and equality cases are identical with their respective signs' (annex 90-91). That is a 'similarly'-type deferral, with no written steps and no formal reduction such as the X -> -X reduction used at annex 78. The multi-step inequality, mean monotonicity and natural-filtration parts are written.

ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C006 (partial): (1) Unstated assumption. The first assertion, 'For predictable bounded H_i, the transform is adapted and integrable at every finite time' (body 107-108), places no hypothesis on X. Its proof needs X adapted and integrable at each time (annex 144-150). Compare body 135-136, where the analogous X_T claim states exactly these hypotheses. (2) The promised submartingale case for H_i>=0 (body 111-112) gets only 'The submartingale case uses the opposite sign' (annex 160). The martingale and supermartingale cases are written.

ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C007 (partial): Unsupported source attribution. The stopped information F_T (body 118-122) is attributed only through the chapter statement at body 9-10: 'The source for the constructions, theorems and exercises developed here is Durrett's Section 4.2', pp. 217-224. Those pages of the held source define a stopping time by {N=n} in F_n (p. 220) and contain no stopped sigma-field. The source first uses F_M in Ex. 4.4.3-4.4.4 (p. 239). The stopping-time and stopped-process parts are supported by p. 220.

ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C008 (partial): Unsupported source attribution. Three assertions are attributed by body 9-10 to Durrett Section 4.2, pp. 217-224: F_T is a sigma-algebra, S<=T implies F_S is contained in F_T, and X_T is F_T-measurable and integrable for bounded T (body 132-136; annex 173-200). Those pages contain only the {N=n} stopping-time definition and Theorem 4.2.9 (p. 220), with no stopped sigma-field. The {T=n} equivalence and stopped-process preservation are written and supported by the source.

ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C009 (partial): (1) Unsupported source attribution. The entry (E(X_T|F_S)=X_S and its inequalities for S<=T<=N, body 145-156) is attributed only by body 9-10 to Durrett Section 4.2, pp. 217-224. No bounded-time sampling theorem and no stopped sigma-field appear on those pages; in the held source this material is Thm 4.4.1 (p. 235) and Ex. 4.4.2-4.4.4 (pp. 238-239). (2) The promised submartingale case is dispatched by 'The submartingale case reverses the inequalities' (annex 243). (3) The step from 'the integral of X_T over A <= the integral of X_S over A, for every A in F_S' to E(X_T|F_S)<=X_S is not written here. It is handed off to 'the bounded-level conditional comparison argument' (annex 239-240). That is a technique written for pointwise order at annex/p15/conditional-expectation.tex 115-127, not a stated result.

ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C011 (partial): Unstated assumption. The alternating times are defined for an arbitrary real process (body 161-168). The entry's first assertion, that the T_j are stopping times and H_m is predictable (body 185-186), comes before and independently of the submartingale hypothesis at body 189. It holds only for adapted X, and its proof uses adaptedness: annex 255 ({T_1<=n} = union of {X_m<=a}, in F_n) and annex 258-260. The held source states this construction for a submartingale (p. 220). The greedy-maximality and clipped-process inequality parts are written.
